newsitem.title: USA: Estate of TV star Audrey Meadows being auctioned.
newsitem.headline: Estate of TV star Audrey Meadows being auctioned.

text.p: She played the wife of a Brooklyn bus driver, but the late actress Audrey Meadows lived the life of a queen of Camelot, according to the Florida auctioneer who will begin to sell her belongings this weekend.

"She probably led the kind of life where she got up in the morning and thought, 'What can I buy today?'" C.B. Charles, whose southeast Florida auction house is disposing of Meadows' possessions beginning Friday night, said Thursday.
Meadows, who died last February, was best known for playing Alice Kramden, the wife of bus driver Ralph Kramden on the hit 1950s television comedy, "The Honeymooners."

But she was the real-life wife of aviation pioneer Robert Six, who founded Continental Airlines and died about 10 years ago. The couple's homes included a Beverly Hills mansion and a ranch in Colorado and their circle included business people and politicians in addition to Hollywood notables.

"He was very much in the in-crowd. He was friendly with all of the presidents. We have a lot of letters, not copies, signed by John F. Kennedy, Jacqueline Kennedy ... Bush, Eisenhower. We even have one from Harry Truman," Charles said.

Meadows' possessions also included boxes of jewelry, paintings, a large wardrobe of designer clothing and mementos including a jewel-encrusted 19th-century Russian cigarette case, a six-foot ivory Chinese sculpture and a box full of Honeymooners scripts.

Charles would not estimate the value of the estate, which he bought from Meadows' heirs. He said one necklace was one of only four copies of a necklace that sold at the Jacqueline Onassis auction for $90,500.

He said there were 800 lots for sale this weekend and there would be many more for sale next month. His firm had had about 10 times as many visitors as usual since the Meadows estate went on display, he said.
